prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1403; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by the third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Both vehicles drivable from scene per initial contact. Claimant reports neck pain and headache and has been evaluated at an urgent care facility, where a concussion was noted. Claimant is now represented by counsel; all further contact to be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office to confirm representation and acknowledge the letter of protection request. Requested medical records and billing from the treating provider, along with prior records for the cervical spine for the past several years. Attorney indicated the claimant has not returned to full work duties and is reporting ongoing dizziness and light sensitivity. Advised that a recorded statement from the claimant can be arranged through counsel only.

Entry 3: Received photos of the rear bumper and trunk area of the insured vehicle from the insured. Photos show a cracked tail light lens and a dented bumper cover. Estimate requested from the repair facility. Third-party vehicle damage appraisal scheduled but not yet completed. Reviewed the police report, which notes the third-party driver stated they were looking at a phone before impact.

Entry 4: Reviewed the treating neurologist's initial consultation notes received through counsel. Diagnosis includes mild traumatic brain injury with post-concussive symptoms. Follow-up imaging ordered. Noted the claimant's prior history of migraines, which counsel has disclosed. Referred file to the medical review unit for an independent records review and to determine whether a nurse case manager should be assigned. Reserve review scheduled for next cycle.

Entry 5: Liability position reviewed with supervisor. Rear impact generally supports the third-party driver's responsibility, but the claimant's counsel has asserted the insured may have braked suddenly, which the insured denies. Dashcam footage from the insured vehicle has been requested to resolve the dispute. Settlement evaluation deferred pending completion of medical treatment and receipt of the neurologist's final report. Next follow-up set for the standard review interval.
